name: Guest IO
description: The two descriptors guest code may write to, and the writing surface it reaches them through.

scenarios.title: Only the captured descriptors may be opened
scenarios.when: guest code constructs an IO over a descriptor outside the captured pair
scenarios.then: the invocation fails with a message naming the descriptor constraint

scenarios.title: Only writing is offered
scenarios.when: guest code constructs an IO in a mode other than write
scenarios.then: the invocation fails with a message naming the mode constraint

scenarios.title: The descriptor is checked where it is used, not only where it was given
given: guest code that reassigned an opened IO's descriptor to another number
scenarios.when: it writes through that IO
scenarios.then: the invocation fails with a message naming the descriptor constraint

scenarios.title: The standard output stream reports its descriptor
scenarios.when: guest code reads the standard output stream's descriptor number
scenarios.then: it is 1

scenarios.title: The standard error stream reports its descriptor
scenarios.when: guest code reads the standard error stream's descriptor number
scenarios.then: it is 2

scenarios.title: Appending answers the stream, so it chains
scenarios.when: guest code appends to the standard output stream
scenarios.then: the append answers that same stream

scenarios.title: A captured stream is not a terminal
scenarios.when: guest code asks the standard output stream whether it is a terminal
scenarios.then: it is not

scenarios.title: A captured stream is synchronous to begin with
scenarios.when: guest code reads the standard output stream's sync flag
scenarios.then: it is true

scenarios.title: Setting the sync flag answers what was assigned
scenarios.when: guest code assigns the standard output stream's sync flag
scenarios.then: the assignment answers the value assigned

scenarios.title: The sync flag keeps what it was set to
given: guest code that turned the standard output stream's sync flag off
scenarios.when: it reads the flag back
scenarios.then: it is false

scenarios.title: Flushing answers the stream
scenarios.when: guest code flushes the standard output stream
scenarios.then: the flush answers that same stream

scenarios.title: A captured stream is open for as long as the invocation runs
scenarios.when: guest code asks the standard output stream whether it is closed
scenarios.then: it is not

scenarios.title: The integer conversion is the descriptor number
scenarios.when: guest code converts the standard output stream to an Integer
scenarios.then: it is the stream's descriptor number

scenarios.title: Appended bytes are captured like written ones
scenarios.when: guest code appends bytes to the standard output stream
scenarios.then: those bytes appear in the output capture

scenarios.title: A short string reaches the capture whole
scenarios.when: guest code prints a string short enough to be stored inline
scenarios.then: the capture holds it byte for byte

scenarios.title: A long string reaches the capture whole
scenarios.when: guest code prints a string too long to be stored inline
scenarios.then: the capture holds it byte for byte

scenarios.title: A payload is bytes, not text up to the first zero
scenarios.when: guest code prints a string containing a zero byte
scenarios.then: the capture holds every byte including the zero

scenarios.title: A string is written as it stands
scenarios.when: guest code prints a String
scenarios.then: the capture holds its bytes unchanged

scenarios.title: Anything else is written as its string form
scenarios.when: guest code prints a value that is not a String
scenarios.then: the capture holds that value's string form

scenarios.title: Formatting applies width and precision
scenarios.when: guest code formats a number with width and precision specifiers
scenarios.then: the invocation answers the formatted String

scenarios.title: A String formats against a list of arguments
scenarios.when: guest code formats a String against an Array of arguments
scenarios.then: the invocation answers the interpolated String

scenarios.title: Formatted printing reaches the capture
scenarios.when: guest code prints with a format string
scenarios.then: the capture holds the formatted bytes

scenarios.title: Putting a character number writes that byte
scenarios.when: guest code puts a character by its number
scenarios.then: the capture holds that one byte

scenarios.title: Putting a character does not touch the error channel
scenarios.when: guest code puts a character
scenarios.then: the error capture is empty

scenarios.title: A character number above a byte is taken modulo a byte
scenarios.when: guest code puts a character by a number larger than a byte
scenarios.then: the capture holds the low byte of that number

scenarios.title: Putting a character answers nothing
scenarios.when: guest code's last expression puts a character
scenarios.then: the invocation answers nothing

scenarios.title: The writing delegators are not callable on a receiver
scenarios.when: guest code calls a writing delegator with an explicit receiver
scenarios.then: the invocation fails with the guest's no-method error

scenarios.title: A refused delegator writes nothing on its way out
scenarios.when: guest code calls a writing delegator with an explicit receiver
scenarios.then: the output capture is empty

scenarios.title: Putting a string writes its first character
scenarios.when: guest code puts a multi-character String
scenarios.then: the capture holds only its first character

scenarios.title: Inspecting writes the inspect form, not the string form
scenarios.when: guest code inspects a Hash to the output stream
scenarios.then: the capture holds the Hash's inspect form

scenarios.title: A long argument list is written to the end
scenarios.when: guest code writes a hundred and fifty arguments in one call
scenarios.then: the capture holds a line for every one of them

scenarios.title: A list is flattened by what it is, not by its class
scenarios.when: guest code writes an instance of an Array subclass
scenarios.then: the capture holds one line per element

text: Guest code can write to two descriptors and no others. The constraint is
witnessed twice — where a stream is opened and where it is written through —
because the descriptor a stream carries is guest-mutable, which makes the
opening check a courtesy on its own.
The rest is fidelity. Bytes go out as bytes: inline and heap strings alike,
zero bytes included, a String unchanged and anything else through its string
form. The supplementary surface is spelled out one member at a time because
a script written against the mruby IO it mirrors expects each of them, and a
single collective assertion would let any one of them drift.
Which channel bytes land in, where they stop, and what survives a failed run
are the host end of this surface and belong with the Sandbox behaviors.
